senses.gloss: (b. h.; Shaf. of קל) [to swing,] to weigh, balance.
units: <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 4">Gen. R. s. 4</cite> <he>הכנס ורחוץ ושְׁקוֹל וכ׳</he> go in and bathe, and weigh thyself before and after &c.; <he>כיון שיצא וש׳ וכ׳</he> when he came out and weighed himself, he had lost nothing.
<cite ref="Mishnah Bava Batra 5:11">B. Bath. V, 11</cite> <he>היה שׁוֹקֵל לוֹ עין בעין</he> if he gave him exact weight, v. <cite ref="P00601"><he>עַיִן</he></cite>.

Ib. 89ᵃ לא יאמר לו שקול … אלא שוקל ליטרא וכ׳ he cannot say to him, weigh me three single fourths of a litra, but he weighs (puts in the balance) one litra, and puts one-fourth of a litra with the meat; a. fr.—Trnsf. to weigh, consider, account.
<cite ref="Kohelet Rabbah 12:14:1">Koh. R. to XII, 14</cite> <he>עבד שרבו שוקל וכ׳</he> a slave to whom his master accounts errors as wilful offenses; <cite ref="Chagigah 5a">Ḥag. 5ᵃ</cite>.

<cite ref="Chagigah 5a:8">Ib.</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Malachi 3:5">Mal. III, 5</cite>) <he>אוי לני שש׳ … קלות וכ׳</he> woe unto us to whom the Scripture accounts light offenses alike with severe crimes; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Nach 589">Yalk. Mal. 589</cite>. Mekh. Yithro, s. 8 <he>חביב … שש׳ כבודן וכ׳</he> the honoring of father and mother is precious before God, for he put their honor and the fear of them on a level with his own honor &c.; (<cite ref="Kiddushin 30b">Kidd. 30ᵇ</cite> <cite ref="U00391"><he>השוה</he></cite>); a. e.

senses.gloss: (denom. of שֶׁקֶל) to offer the head-tax (half a Shekel).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 1:4">Shek. I, 4</cite> <he>כל כהן ששוקל וכ׳</he> a priest that pays the head-tax.
<cite ref="Mishnah Shekalim 1:6">Ib. 6</cite> <he>השוקל על ידי וכ׳</he> if one pays the head-tax for a priest, a woman, or a minor, he is exempt (from paying agio).
Ned. IV, 2 (33ᵃ) את שקלו (לו)שוקל may pay the head-tax for him; a. fr.—In gen. to pay taxes.
Tosef. Dem. VI, 3; 4; Y. ib. VI, end, 26ᵃ, v. אוֹצָר.—Part. pass. שָׁקוּל; f. שְׁקוּלָה; pl. שְׁקוּלִים, שְׁקוּלִין; שְׁקוּלוֹת even-balanced, of equal importance.

<cite ref="Sanhedrin 3b:3">Snh. 3ᵇ</cite>, a. fr. <he>אין בית דין ש׳</he> a court must never be even-balanced, i.e. not be of even numbers, opp. <he>נוטה</he>; v. <cite ref="B00753"><he>בַּיִת</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 18:20">Num. R. s. 18<sup>8</sup></cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Psalms 99:6">Ps. XCIX, 6</cite>) <he>שמואל שש׳ כנגד וכ׳</he> Samuel who is balanced against Moses and Aaron together; <cite ref="Berakhot 31b:17">Ber. 31ᵇ</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="I Samuel 1:11">I Sam. I, 11</cite>, <he>זרע אנשים</he>) <he>זרע שש׳ כנגד שני אנשים וכ׳</he> a seed (son) that will hold the balance against two men &c. Ib. 33ᵃ <he>מזכירין … שש׳ כתחיית וכ׳</he> we insert ‘the power of rain’ (v. <cite ref="C00062"><he>גְּבוּרָה</he></cite>) in the section about resurrection, because it is equal to resurrection.

<cite ref="Bava Kamma 3a:13">B. Kam. 3ᵃ</cite> <he>ש׳ הן וכ׳</he> they (the two kinds of damages) are even-balanced (you cannot decide between the two), let both be included; <cite ref="Zevachim 4b:18">Zeb. 4ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Nazir 58b:8">Naz. 58ᵇ</cite> <he>ש׳ הוא</he> the balance is even; <cite ref="Arakhin 4b:70">Arakh. 4ᵇ</cite>. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., ch. XVII, Par. 14; <cite ref="Yalkut Shimoni on Torah 462:2">Yalk. Lev. 462</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Leviticus 3:4">Lev. III, 4</cite>) <he>הדבר ש׳ יטול וכ׳</he> it may be understood either way, he should take that part of the midriff which is by the liver, or a portion of the liver with the midriff &c.; a. fr.
Gen. R. s. 59 (ref. to Hos. XII, 8) that is Eliezer, שהיה יושב ומַשְׁקִיל את בתו וכ׳ for he sat and pondered on his daughter: is she or is she not worthy?; Yalk. Hos. 528 ומְשַׁקֵּל (Pi.).
